cards.title: IUPAC Gold Book — hybridization
claims: Hybridization is a linear combination of atomic orbitals on an atom; hybrid-orbital labels are model vocabulary rather than a molecular-shape observation by itself.
cards.access_note: Verified 2026-10-04 against the current IUPAC Gold Book term page/plain endpoint; definition identifies hybridization as linear combination of atomic orbitals on an atom.

cards.title: OpenStax Chemistry 2e §7.6 Molecular Structure and Polarity
claims: Two/three/four regions of electron density map to linear/trigonal-planar/tetrahedral electron-pair geometries.
Electron-pair geometry includes bonds and lone pairs, while molecular structure names atom positions.
NH3 has tetrahedral electron-pair geometry with trigonal-pyramidal molecular structure.

cards.title: OpenStax Chemistry 2e §8.2 Hybrid Atomic Orbitals
claims: Three regions correspond to the introductory sp2 model with three sp2 hybrids and one unhybridized p orbital.
A multiple bond counts as one region of electron density.
Four regions correspond to the introductory sp3 model.
cards.access_note: Verified 2026-10-04: OpenStax Chemistry 2e §8.2 states three regions give three sp2 hybrids plus one unhybridized p orbital, and a multiple bond counts as one region of electron density.

cards.title: OpenStax Chemistry §8.1 Valence Bond Theory
claims: Sigma overlap lies along the internuclear axis.
Pi bonding arises from side-by-side p-orbital overlap.
A double bond contains one sigma and one pi component; a triple bond contains one sigma and two pi components.
cards.access_note: Verified 2026-10-04: OpenStax Chemistry 2e §8.1/§8.3 distinguishes sigma overlap along the internuclear axis from side-by-side pi overlap and gives double/triple bond sigma-pi compositions.
